title: The Appointments Clause and permissible appointing actors
shortTitle: The Appointments Clause and permissible appointing actors
summary: The Appointments Clause specifies how officers of the United States are appointed and permits alternative methods for inferior officers.
notes:
The default method is presidential nomination and appointment with Senate advice and consent. Congress may by law vest appointment of inferior officers in the President alone, courts of law, or department heads. The initial classification asks whether the position is an office rather than employment; the next asks whether the officer is principal or inferior.

Buckley excludes congressional leaders and an additional House confirmation requirement from the permitted methods for officials exercising significant federal authority. Freytag addresses what qualifies as a court of law or department. Morrison permits interbranch appointment where the arrangement does not impair constitutional functions or create an incongruity between judicial work and the appointment responsibility. Article II’s appointment language, reproduced at printed147, does not impose the two-thirds Senate threshold mentioned in the chapter’s introductory printed135 sentence; that introductory statement should not be used as the governing rule.
